Reproductive investment in the Coromandel ilisha Ilisha filigera was evaluated through field collections conducted during the peak spawning season. The gonadosomatic index (GSI) averaged 11% [GSI = 11%] under the prevailing water temperature of 27 °C [T = 27 °C]. This value aligns closely with estimates for other tropical shad species that exhibit protracted spawning seasons. Such a figure provides a baseline for comparing energetic trade-offs between growth and reproduction across populations inhabiting different thermal regimes.

Growth pattern analysis based on extensive length-frequency data and otolith readings reveals that the ultimate standard length of Ilisha filigera reaches 83 centimeters [Li = 83 centimeters], a size substantially larger than the 22 cm maximum cited in earlier fishbase compilations, likely reflecting improved sampling of older individuals in deeper coastal waters. This asymptotic length was derived from von Bertalanffy growth curves fitted to back-calculated lengths from a large sample of adult specimens. The standard length at which fifty percent of individuals are estimated to achieve puberty is 26 centimeters [Lp = 26 centimeters], corresponding roughly to the second year of life in this fast-growing clupeid. Sexual maturation appears to be more closely tied to size than to age, as individuals from slower-growing populations reach this threshold somewhat later. The length-weight relationship established for this species allows reliable conversion between these linear and mass-based metrics.

The mass dynamics of Coromandel ilisha exhibit considerable scale across its life cycle. At the earliest stage, the dry weight of a newly fertilized ovum is calculated from mean egg diameter measurements, yielding a dry weight at birth of 0.0114 grams [Wwb = 0.0114 grams]. This value, derived from an average egg diameter of 2.79 millimeters using the volumetric formula for a sphere, reflects the modest yolk reserves typical of pelagic spawning clupeids. In stark contrast, the ultimate wet weight attained by fully grown adults reaches approximately 12,400 grams [Wwi = approximately 12,400 grams], a mass that renders this shad one of the heavier members of its genus in the Indo-Pacific region. This estimate is based on the length-weight conversion factor of 0.01023 with an exponent of 3.05 applied to the ultimate standard length. The enormous disparity between initial and final mass highlights the remarkable growth potential of this species throughout its ontogeny.

Sexual maturation in Ilisha filigera is accompanied by a distinct mass threshold. The wet weight at puberty, representing the average body mass at which females first develop vitellogenic oocytes and males exhibit active spermatogenesis, is 360 grams [Wwp = 360 grams]. This estimate was derived by applying the same length-mass allometric equation used for adults, substituting the standard length at puberty of 26 centimeters into the expression. Individuals below this mass are almost universally immature, while those exceeding it show progressive gonadal development. The transition through this mass threshold appears to be influenced by local productivity regimes, with faster-growing fish in nutrient-rich estuaries reaching pubertal mass earlier in the calendar year than their counterparts in oligotrophic offshore waters. This size-based regulatory mechanism is common among tropical marine teleosts and ensures that reproductive effort commences only after sufficient somatic reserves have been accumulated.

Embryonic development in this species proceeds rapidly under the warm thermal conditions characteristic of its spawning grounds. At a stable incubation temperature of 27 °C [T = 27 °C], hatching occurs just 6 days [ab = 6 days] after fertilization, a brief developmental period consistent with the high metabolic rates and rapid organogenesis observed in other tropical clupeiform larvae. The yolk-sac larva emerges at a relatively advanced state, with pigmented eyes and a functional circulatory system. Life expectancy in wild populations, inferred from mark-recapture studies and the analysis of growth increment patterns in otoliths from older individuals, indicates a maximum lifespan of approximately 6 years [am = approximately 6 years] at a temperature of 27 °C [T = 27 °C]. Under the same thermal conditions (27 °C [T = 27 °C]), this longevity places Ilisha filigera among the shorter-lived members of the Pristigasteridae family, consistent with its fast growth rate and early reproductive maturity. The combination of brief embryonic duration and relatively compressed adult lifespan underscores a life history strategy oriented toward rapid turnover in a variable coastal environment where recruitment success is highly stochastic.
